authority.legal_name: Government of the Maldives (Ministry of Transport) with MTCC operating the Raajje Transport Link (RTL) integrated national ferry & bus network
authority.geography_type: an atoll nation of ~190 inhabited islands scattered across 20 administrative atolls, separated by open Indian Ocean channels and lagoon waters

mandate.summary: The Maldives is building the Raajje Transport Link (RTL) — an integrated national ferry and bus network operated by MTCC to connect every inhabited island so that citizens (not just resort guests) can reach hospitals, schools, jobs and family affordably. The network is rolling out atoll-by-atoll on a diesel fleet; the mandate is universal, affordable, sustainable public connectivity for the nation.
current_priorities: Extending RTL ferry service to the remaining atolls to connect all ~190 inhabited islands
Affordable, reliable public inter-island mobility for residents — not resort transfers
Decarbonizing the public fleet, consistent with the Maldives' climate commitments

policy_targets.interim_target: The Maldives has pledged national net-zero (conditional) and is among the world's most sea-level-vulnerable states; a zero-emission public fleet is a strategic climate alignment, not a nicety
policy_targets.vision: A fast, reliable, efficient, affordable, convenient AND sustainable public transport network for the whole nation (RTL mandate)
policy_targets.relevance: A zero-emission foiling fleet advances the Maldives' climate commitments while making the public RTL crossings faster and cheaper to run — decarbonizing the exact mobility citizens depend on, in the nation with the most to lose from sea-level rise.

precedent.headline: The national public ferry network already exists and is expanding atoll-by-atoll.

existing_program.program: Integrated national high-speed ferry & bus network; zone-by-zone rollout (Zones already live include the northern Ha/Hdh/Sh atolls, Lh atoll, and the southern Ga/Gdh atolls), extending toward all 20 atolls
existing_program.proof_stat: A live, government-backed public ferry network connecting inhabited islands 7 days a week — the platform the foiling fleet decarbonizes and accelerates
existing_program.note: This is a PUBLIC network for residents; resort transfers are explicitly out of scope for this authority proposal.

interpretation_for_navier: The Maldives proposal must be the PUBLIC RTL network — inhabited-island connectivity for citizens — NOT resort transfers. The prior draft led with resort jetties (Soneva Fushi, Six Senses, Baros); that is the wrong authority frame and is corrected here. Anchor on the confident Greater Malé public corridors (Malé–Hulhumalé–Villimalé and the Kaafu local-island runs), then frame the national RTL zone rollout as the authority's reach. Do not mint speculative precise corridors in distant atolls.

domestic_network.note: Candidate boarding points with APPROXIMATE anchor coordinates [lng, lat] — Greater Malé region public terminals (high confidence). Precise berths and routed geometry are Grok's to seal. Distant-atoll RTL corridors are described in the narrative, NOT minted here, to avoid confidently-wrong geography.

domestic_pairs.rationale: The capital-region public ferry backbone — Malé to Hulhumalé, the nation's highest-volume public crossing; fast, quiet, zero-emission.
Short high-frequency Malé–Villimalé commuter hop; ideal for quiet electric foiling.
Malé to Maafushi, a large inhabited local island — a core resident and public connection across South Malé atoll waters.
Malé to Gulhi inhabited-island public run; RTL-style community connectivity.
Malé to Guraidhoo inhabited island — longer South Malé atoll public leg.
Malé to Thilafushi — essential worker/industrial public connection across the lagoon.
Hulhumalé to Thulusdhoo, a North Malé atoll inhabited island — extends the public network beyond the capital.

regional_links.note: The proposal stands on the domestic RTL public network. No cross-border regional link is minted; the Colombo↔Malé idea from the prior draft is not a public RTL corridor and is excluded.

routing_hazards.instruction: Route every leg through open lagoon/channel water to charted island jetties — never straight-line across reefs or islands. Provide explicit hand waypoints around atoll reef rings and the Malé commercial anchorage.

hazards.hazard: Atoll reef rings and shallow lagoons
hazards.detail: Every inhabited island sits within a reef ring; approaches are shallow and reef-fringed. Route to charted channel entrances (Maafushi, Gulhi, Guraidhoo, Thulusdhoo), never straight-line to shore.
Malé's harbour and outer anchorage are congested with cargo, dhonis and public ferries; depart via the charted public-ferry channel.
Longer legs (Guraidhoo, Thulusdhoo) cross open, current-swept channels between atoll rims; weather- and current-aware routing.
The Maldives has protected reefs and marine areas; low-wake foiling is an advantage but observe protected zones and dive sites.
